newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - March 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
GOVERNOR WILL NOT BE REMOVED, SAYS PRIME MINISTER

The prime minister has virtually ruled out the dismissal of the Uttar Pradesh governor. In an obvious reference to the murder of an opposition legislator in the state, he said action could not be taken for one murder. He said a comparative study of the last five years since the demolition of the Babri mosque would have to be done before assessing the law and order situation in the state.
The Hindustan Times
PREMIER DARES OPPOSITION TO MOVE NO-CONFIDENCE MOTION

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda dared the opposition to bring a no-confidence motion in parliament implicating him or his ministers in any scam. He was replying to a debate in the lower house on the motion of thanks to the president's address to the joint sitting of parliament. He said he would quit if found guilty and sack his ministers in the event of their involvement being proved in any corruption case.
The Pioneer
ATONNC ENERGY DEPARTMENT BUYS WASTE FOR 23 BLN RUPEES

A parliamentary committee called for a detailed investigation into the purchases of equipment worth over 23 billion rupees by the Department of Atomic Energy (DAE) for setting up nuclear power plants across the country. The equipment was bought by the DAE as part of the government's ambitious plan to generate 10,000 megawatts of nuclear power by 2000. But with the power generation target slashed to 3,320 megawatts and the deadline extended to 2004, the equipment, according to the DAE, was rendered useless.
The Economic Times
BOURSES STILL IN BULL GRIP

The correction in share prices, after a 14 percent rise in the benchmark index over four trading sessions, continued to elude marketmen. For the second day, the Bombay bourse index came very close to the 4,000 mark before closing at 3,944.61, up 73 points from its previous close.
BILL GATES OPTIMISTIC ON INDIA

For Microsoft, India was a more important investment destination than China. This was stated by Bill Gates, the chairman and chief executive officer of Microsoft Corporation, in an interview. Gates was, however, noncommittal on making India one of the locations for Microsoft software development. He said they had done all their development in one location, which had proved very efficient for them.
INDIVIDUALS TO TAKE HOME MORE IN ALLOWANCES, CAPITAL GAINS

The expert panel on recasting the income tax act has focused on providing incentives to employees of companies by liberalising the tax incidence on allowances. Individuals could now look forward to taking home more of their remuneration packages and profits from investments. The panel suggested a complete shift in formula for computation of capital gains to a block of assets concept. It also suggested increasing tax deduction limits for medical and leave travel allowances. Several tax incentives for professionals were also on the list.
Financial Express
MAJOR RELIEFS FOR EXPORT UNITS

The government conceded a major relief to hundred percent export-oriented units and those set up in export processing and free trade zones. These units can now sell finished products, waste or scrap made wholly of indigenous raw materials in the domestic tariff area (DTA) by paying excise duty only. A Finance Ministry notification said the excise duty payable would be on the lines applicable to units in the DTA.
CORPORATES MAY HOLD ADVANCE TAX FOR VOLUNTARY DISCLOSURES

Tax departments feared the advance tax collection for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) would fall by at least 25 percent on account of the newly introduced voluntary disclosure scheme (VDS). Bombay alone would see a five billion rupee shortfall as many assessees were likely to shift the tax liability from the current fiscal to 1997/98. The targeted income-tax collections for 1996/97 was 47 billion rupees against 37 billion in the previous year. With the VDS coming into force, the revenue may not even reach 43 billion rupees, sources added.
Business Standard
COST OF DISCLOSING FUNDS ABROAD PUT AT 17.5 PCT

Cost of disclosing funds stashed overseas would be nearly 40 percent lower than what was indicated in the voluntary disclosure scheme announced in the budget. The effective cost, after paying a 30 percent income tax as stipulated in the scheme, would be 17.5 percent, the rate at which most banks and financial institutions lend funds.
FOREIGN INSTITUTIONS AMONG TOP IDBI SHAREHOLDERS

Three domestic companies made way for an equal number of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) in the list of top 10 Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI) shareholders. Essar Steel, Nagarjuna Fertilisers and Syndicate Bank were the three domestic firms which sold their holdings in the bank. Merrill Lynch Pacific Fund with 2.9 million shares, Foreign and Colonial Emerging Markets with 2.39 million shares and Schroder India (Mauritius) with 1.92 million shares were the three FIIs which joined the top 10 list.
$300 MILLION RBI INTERVENTION TO ARREST RUPEE RISE

The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) intervened in the foreign exchange (forex) market to buy $300 million over the past two days. It simultaneously mopped up more than 4.25 billion rupees from the money market over the past three days. The intervention in the forex market was aimed at preventing the rupee from appreciating, while the intervention in the money market through open market operations was aimed at picking up the funds released in as a result of the forex intervention.
APPROVAL FOR UNLIMITED FIRMS GIVES TAX BREAKS TO US MAJORS

American transnationals operating in India would reap tax benefits in the United States following the recommendation of the expert panel on the Companies Act to retain legal provisions for unlimited companies. U.S. laws provide a three percent tax shield on profits earned from investments abroad. Many U.S.-based multinationals with heavy investment commitments in India were actively lobbying against the government's earlier plan to phase out legal provisions for unlimited companies.
Business Line
SUGAR PRODUCTION TOUCHES 5.5 MLN TONNES

Total production of sugar in the current season ended January 31, 1997 was 5.52 million tonnes, the food minister informed parliament. The minister said of this, 450,000 tonnes had been allowed for general export in instalments. He said the total stock of sugar as on December 7 last was 6.5 million tonnes.
